name: NJ-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Herb Conaway holds a D+5 district with a strong fundraising edge
Challenger Michael McGuire has raised under $80,000 with almost no cash on hand
Prediction markets price the Democratic incumbent near 98% to win
No independent or third-party candidates show meaningful financial support
model.rationale: Conaway combines incumbency, a favorable district lean, and a lopsided money advantage — roughly $439,000 on hand versus under $1,000 for McGuire — while markets price him near certain to win. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Conaway or an unexpected polling miss in this district would be the main signals to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Herb Conaway, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a New Jersey district that leans Democratic by about five points. He has raised over $930,000 and holds roughly $439,000 in cash, while Republican Michael McGuire has raised under $80,000 and reports just $807 on hand. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and third-party candidates on the ballot show no visible financial backing.

Prediction markets give Conaway about a 98 percent chance of winning, and the fundamentals point the same direction: the district lean, incumbency, and the money gap all favor the Democrat. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on these structural advantages, which point to a comfortable double-digit win for Conaway.
